quests.instruction: Which shape has two pairs of parallel sides?
quests.hint: Look for a shape where both pairs of opposite sides run side by side.
quests.explanation: In a rhombus, each side is parallel to the side across from it, so there are two pairs. A trapezoid has just one pair and a triangle has none.
quests.funFact: A four-sided shape with two pairs of parallel sides is called a parallelogram.

quests.instruction: How many pairs of parallel sides does a regular hexagon have?
quests.hint: Each side of a regular hexagon runs alongside the side directly across from it.
quests.explanation: A regular hexagon has six sides, and each one is parallel to the side directly across from it. Six sides in pairs make three pairs.
quests.funFact: A stop sign, which is a regular octagon, has four pairs of parallel sides.

quests.instruction: Which shape has no parallel sides at all?
quests.hint: Parallel sides never meet. Check whether any two sides could be stretched forever without crossing.
quests.explanation: If you stretch any two sides of a triangle, they cross at a corner, so no two sides are parallel. A rectangle has two pairs and a regular hexagon has three.
quests.funFact: Lines that are not parallel will cross each other somewhere if they are extended far enough.

quests.instruction: In a diagram, one circle holds shapes with four sides and another circle holds shapes with all sides equal. Where does a rectangle with two long sides and two short sides go?
options: In the overlap of both circles
quests.hint: Check the rectangle against each rule, one at a time.
quests.explanation: The rectangle has four sides, so it fits the first circle. Its sides are not all equal, so it does not fit the second circle.
quests.funFact: Venn diagrams are named after John Venn, an English mathematician who used them in the 1880s.

quests.instruction: Four shapes are listed: square, rhombus, rectangle, and kite. The rule is four equal sides and four square corners. How many of these shapes follow the rule?
quests.hint: A shape has to pass both parts of the rule.
quests.explanation: Only the square has four equal sides and four square corners. A rhombus can lean, a rectangle can have long and short sides, and a kite has two different pairs of sides.
quests.funFact: Venn diagrams can have three overlapping circles as well as two.

quests.instruction: A diagram has one circle for shapes with four sides and one circle for shapes with a curved edge. Which shape would sit outside both circles?
quests.hint: Find a shape that fails both rules.
quests.explanation: A pentagon has five sides and no curved edge, so it fits neither circle. A square fits the first circle and a semicircle fits the second.
quests.funFact: The box around the circles in a Venn diagram stands for everything being sorted, including shapes that fit neither circle.

quests.instruction: In a guessing game, the clues are only straight sides, an odd number of sides, and more than three sides. Which shape is it?
quests.hint: Use the clues one at a time to remove choices.
quests.explanation: A hexagon and a rectangle have an even number of sides. A pentagon has five, which is odd and more than three.
quests.funFact: Guessing games with yes-or-no clues are a good way to practice sorting by properties.

quests.instruction: The clues are four sides and exactly one pair of parallel sides. Which shape is it?
quests.hint: Count the pairs of parallel sides in each choice.
quests.explanation: A rectangle and a rhombus both have two pairs of parallel sides. A trapezoid has only one pair.
quests.funFact: The two parallel sides of a trapezoid are called its bases.

quests.instruction: Which fact helps you tell a rhombus apart from a kite?
quests.correctAnswer: A rhombus has all four sides equal
options: A rhombus has all four sides equal
quests.hint: Look for a fact that is true for a rhombus but not for an ordinary kite.
quests.explanation: Both shapes have four sides and four corners. Only the rhombus must have all four sides equal, while a kite has two different pairs.
quests.funFact: The two lines joining opposite corners of a kite cross at a square corner.

quests.instruction: Mia drew three four-sided shapes. A has four equal sides and square corners. B has four equal sides and leaning corners. C has two long and two short sides with square corners. Which two are both rectangles?
quests.hint: A rectangle needs four square corners.
quests.explanation: A and C both have four square corners, so both are rectangles, and A is a special rectangle with equal sides. B has leaning corners, so it is not a rectangle.
quests.funFact: Mathematicians sort shapes into families so they can prove facts about many shapes at once.

quests.instruction: Which pair always looks exactly alike except for size?
quests.hint: Think about whether making one bigger or smaller could ever turn it into the other.
quests.explanation: Every square has four equal sides and square corners, so a bigger square is just a smaller one scaled up. Rectangles can be long or squat, and rhombuses can lean by different amounts.
quests.funFact: A photocopier can enlarge a square and it stays a square.

quests.instruction: A triangle, a square, a pentagon, and a hexagon are sorted by whether they have an even or odd number of sides. How many have an even number of sides?
quests.hint: Write the number of sides for each shape first.
quests.explanation: The square has 4 sides and the hexagon has 6, which are both even. The triangle has 3 and the pentagon has 5, which are odd.
quests.funFact: Even numbers always end in 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8.

quests.instruction: A woodworker has a rectangular piece, an L-shaped piece, and a triangular piece. Which piece has the most corners?
quests.hint: Walk around each outline and count every turn.
quests.explanation: The L-shaped outline has six corners, the rectangle has four, and the triangle has three.
quests.funFact: Many kitchens use L-shaped counters so two walls can share one work space.

quests.instruction: A tile maker cuts a regular hexagon, a square, and a triangle. Which tile has the most pairs of parallel sides?
quests.hint: Count the pairs of sides that face each other and run side by side.
quests.explanation: A regular hexagon has three pairs of parallel sides, a square has two, and a triangle has none.
quests.funFact: Triangles, squares, and hexagons are the only regular shapes that can cover a floor by themselves with no gaps.

quests.instruction: A craft store has two bins: Bin 1 for shapes with only straight sides and Bin 2 for shapes with at least one curved edge. Which bin does a semicircle go in?
quests.hint: Check whether a semicircle has any curved edge at all.
quests.explanation: A semicircle has one curved edge and one straight edge. Because it has at least one curve, it goes in Bin 2.
quests.funFact: A semicircle is exactly half of a circle, cut along a straight line through the center.

quests.instruction: Which statement about a trapezoid and a rectangle is true?
quests.correctAnswer: A rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides; a trapezoid has one
options: Both have exactly one pair of parallel sides
A rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides; a trapezoid has one
A trapezoid has more sides than a rectangle
quests.hint: Count the pairs of parallel sides in each shape.
quests.explanation: A rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides, while a trapezoid has just one pair. Both shapes have four sides.
quests.funFact: Many lampshades have sides shaped like trapezoids.

quests.instruction: A group contains a square, a rectangle, a rhombus, a kite, and a trapezoid. What is the best name for the whole group?
quests.hint: Count the sides on every shape in the group.
quests.explanation: All five shapes have four sides, and four-sided shapes are called quadrilaterals.
quests.funFact: A quadrangle on a school campus is a four-sided courtyard.

quests.instruction: Which group contains only polygons that are not quadrilaterals?
quests.hint: Quadrilaterals have four sides. Avoid any group that includes a four-sided shape.
quests.explanation: A triangle, a pentagon, and a hexagon are polygons with three, five, and six sides. The other groups are all four-sided.
quests.funFact: A polygon with twelve sides is called a dodecagon.

quests.instruction: A box holds 2 triangles, 3 squares, 1 pentagon, and 2 circles. How many of the shapes have only straight sides?
quests.hint: Leave out the shapes with curved edges, then count the rest.
quests.explanation: The 2 triangles, 3 squares, and 1 pentagon have only straight sides, which makes 6. The 2 circles are curved.
quests.funFact: Counting items by kind is the first step in making a tally chart or a bar chart.

quests.instruction: A teacher sorts shapes into two groups. The curved group has a circle, an oval, and a crescent. The straight group has a triangle, a square, a hexagon, and a kite. Which group is bigger, and by how many?
quests.hint: Count the shapes in each group, then compare.
quests.explanation: The straight group has 4 shapes and the curved group has 3, so the straight group is bigger by 1.
quests.funFact: Man-made objects like windows, doors, and books mostly have straight edges.

quests.instruction: Ten shapes are on a shelf: 6 have four sides, 3 have three sides, and 1 has five sides. How many do not have four sides?
quests.hint: Add up the shapes that are not four-sided.
quests.explanation: The 3 three-sided shapes and the 1 five-sided shape are not four-sided, and 3 + 1 = 4. You could also take 6 away from 10.
quests.funFact: Taking a part away from a total, like 10 − 6, is a quick way to count what is left over.

quests.instruction: Tom says all shapes with four sides have two pairs of parallel sides. Which shape proves him wrong?
quests.hint: Find a four-sided shape that has fewer than two pairs.
quests.explanation: A trapezoid has four sides but only one pair of parallel sides. A rhombus and a rectangle each have two pairs.
quests.funFact: Showing one example that breaks a rule is enough to prove the rule wrong.

quests.instruction: Nora says a shape with curved edges cannot have corners. Which shape proves her wrong?
quests.hint: Find a shape that has a curved edge and also a corner.
quests.explanation: A heart has curved edges and also corners at its dip and its point. A circle and an oval have no corners, so they fit Nora's rule.
quests.funFact: Scientists test ideas the same way, by looking for one case that breaks the rule.

quests.instruction: Ravi says: The bigger a shape is, the more corners it has. Which pair proves him wrong?
quests.correctAnswer: A huge square and a small hexagon
options: A small triangle and a huge pentagon
A huge square and a small hexagon
A small hexagon and a huge octagon
quests.hint: Look for the pair where the bigger shape has fewer corners.
quests.explanation: The huge square has 4 corners, but the small hexagon has 6, so the bigger shape has fewer. In the other pairs the bigger shape has more.
quests.funFact: A shape's number of corners depends on its form, not on its size.

quests.instruction: A sorting tree asks two questions: Does the shape have a curved edge? Does it have four sides? How would a hexagon answer?
options: Yes to the first, no to the second
quests.hint: Think about the edges of a hexagon, then count its sides.
quests.explanation: A hexagon has only straight sides, so the first answer is no. It has six sides, not four, so the second answer is no.
quests.funFact: Computers and doctors use yes-or-no sorting trees like this to make decisions.

quests.instruction: A different sorting tree asks: Is it a polygon? If yes, does it have more than five sides? Which shape ends up as a polygon with more than five sides?
quests.hint: Both answers have to be yes.
quests.explanation: An octagon is a polygon with eight sides. A pentagon has exactly five, not more, and a semicircle is not a polygon because it has a curved edge.
quests.funFact: Yes-or-no questions can split any group of shapes into smaller and smaller groups.

quests.instruction: A kite and a trapezoid are both in a pile of four-sided shapes. A worker moves every shape with a pair of parallel sides into a new pile. Which shape stays behind if the kite is an ordinary one?
quests.hint: Check which of the two has a pair of sides that run side by side.
quests.explanation: A trapezoid has one pair of parallel sides, so it moves to the new pile. An ordinary kite has no parallel sides, so it stays behind.
quests.funFact: People have flown kites for over two thousand years.

quests.instruction: Which group has shapes that all have four sides and at least one pair of parallel sides?
quests.hint: A shape must pass both rules, so check each one in a group.
quests.explanation: A square, a rhombus, and a trapezoid each have four sides and parallel sides. An ordinary kite has no parallel sides, and a triangle has only three sides.
quests.funFact: The word trapezoid comes from a Greek word meaning table.

quests.instruction: Eli sorted four shapes. Group A has a square, a rectangle, and a kite. Group B has a triangle and a hexagon. He says Group A is shapes with four equal sides. What did he get wrong?
quests.correctAnswer: A rectangle and a kite do not always have four equal sides
options: A rectangle and a kite do not always have four equal sides
quests.hint: Test his rule on each shape in Group A, not just the first one.
quests.explanation: A square has four equal sides, but a rectangle can have long and short sides and a kite has two different pairs. A better rule for Group A is that every shape has four sides.
quests.funFact: Careful sorters check every item against the rule, not just the first one.

quests.instruction: Which shape could belong to all three groups: four sides, parallel sides, and all sides equal?
quests.hint: Remember which four-sided shapes always have equal sides.
quests.explanation: A rhombus has four sides, two pairs of parallel sides, and four equal sides. A trapezoid does not have equal sides, and an ordinary kite has no parallel sides.
quests.funFact: Rhombus patterns on tiles can make a floor look like stacked cubes.
